steps.title: Analyse the problem and recall relevant learning outcomes
steps.description:
We must evaluate the definite integral ∫₀^{π/8} x sin(2x) dx.
Givens:
 • Integrand: x·sin(2x).
 • Limits of integration: 0 to π/8.
Relevant topics from the first-year Mathematical Methods curriculum:
 • INTEGRATION—CONTINUED → ‘find integrals using integration by parts’. The integrand is a product of a simple algebraic factor (x) and a trigonometric function (sin 2x), the classic setting for integration by parts.
 • FUNCTIONS AND DIFFERENTIATION → familiarity with basic trigonometric identities and derivatives is assumed (we need d/dx[cos 2x] = –2 sin 2x, etc.).
steps.hints:
1. Which factor should be picked for u and which for dv in integration by parts so that the remaining integral is simpler?
2. Remember to evaluate the antiderivative at both limits.

steps.title: Choose the technique and set up integration by parts
steps.description:
Let
  u = x               (so that du = dx)
  dv = sin(2x) dx     (so that v = ∫ sin(2x) dx = –cos(2x)/2).
Using ∫ u dv = u v – ∫ v du, the integral becomes
  ∫₀^{π/8} x sin(2x) dx = [x·(–cos(2x)/2)]₀^{π/8} – ∫₀^{π/8} (–cos(2x)/2)·dx.
steps.hints: Carefully compute v; a factor 1/2 appears because ∫ sin(2x) dx = –cos(2x)/2.

steps.title: Simplify the remaining integral
steps.description:
The first term is –x cos(2x)/2 evaluated at the limits.
The second term becomes +(1/2)∫₀^{π/8} cos(2x)
   = (1/2) · [sin(2x)/2]₀^{π/8}
   = sin(2x)/4 |₀^{π/8}.
steps.hints: Check that the sign in front of the second integral flips because we subtract (–cos …).

steps.title: Evaluate the antiderivative at the bounds
steps.description:
Write the combined antiderivative:
  F(x) = –x cos(2x)/2 + sin(2x)/4.
Upper limit x = π/8:
  cos(2x) = cos(π/4) = √2/2,
  sin(2x) = sin(π/4) = √2/2.
  F(π/8) = –(π/8)(√2/2)/2 + (√2/2)/4
         = –π√2/32 + √2/8
         = √2(4 – π)/32.
Lower limit x = 0:
  cos(0) = 1,  sin(0) = 0
  F(0) = –0·1/2 + 0 = 0.
Therefore the definite integral equals F(π/8) – F(0) = √2(4 – π)/32.
steps.hints: Convert both terms to the common denominator 32 to combine them neatly.

steps.title: Check result and relate back to learning outcomes
steps.description:
• Sign check: x ≥ 0 and sin(2x) ≥ 0 on [0, π/8], so the integral must be positive. Since 4 – π ≈ 0.86 > 0, √2(4 – π)/32 is indeed positive.
• Curriculum connection:
  – Used ‘integration by parts’ (Integration—Continued).
  – Applied trigonometric differentiation inside the parts formula (Functions and Differentiation).
steps.hints: A quick numerical approximation (≈0.038) confirms the plausibility of the exact result.

final_solution:
The definite integral evaluates to
  ∫₀^{π/8} x sin(2x) dx = √2(4 – π)/32.
